title: Course Schedule
description: Given numCourses and a list of prerequisite pairs [a, b] meaning b must be taken before a, return whether it is possible to finish all courses.

reference.use_case: Checking whether a set of tasks with prerequisites can all be completed, i.e. that no chain of requirements loops back on itself.
system_examples: Build systems (Make, Bazel) — ordering targets by dependencies and reporting dependency cycles
Package managers (npm, apt) — resolving install order and detecting circular dependencies
Apache Airflow — validating that a workflow has no cycles before scheduling its tasks
reference.explanation: Model prerequisites as a directed graph; finishing is possible exactly when the graph is acyclic. Kahn's algorithm (in-degree BFS) or DFS with visiting/visited states detects cycles in O(V + E) and yields a valid order. Topological sorting is the core of build tools, schedulers, and migration runners.
